summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR142 crore (up ~80% YoY), but EBITDA margin fell to 9.96% on March raw material spike.
summary.overview: Captain Polyplast reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR142 crore in Q4 FY26 versus INR79.1 crore a year earlier, driven by micro-irrigation and solar pump demand. Q4 EBITDA rose 66% to INR14.16 crore, but margin slipped 86 bps YoY to 9.96%, which management attributed to a sharp March raw material price increase. FY26 total income was INR419 crore (up 44%), with EBITDA of INR6.32 crore at an 11.03% margin as stated. The Ahmedabad plant is now operational and the company's credit rating was upgraded during FY26. Management is focused on shifting mix toward solar EPC and non-subsidy micro-irrigation to improve working capital.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR79.1 crore in Q4 FY25, ~80% YoY

segments.name: Micro-irrigation
segments.commentary: Core business, still mostly subsidy-driven; cash/non-subsidy sales were ~15% of micro-irrigation revenue in FY26. Export contribution is ~5% of micro-irrigation revenue, targeted to reach double digits in five years.

segments.name: Solar pumps (EPC)
segments.commentary: Maharashtra order of ~1,500 pumps in FY26 was the first year in that state; a new 500-pump order worth ~INR11 crore came in Q4. Management says pump EBITDA margin is similar to micro-irrigation.

segments.name: Solar rooftop (EPC)
segments.commentary: Added multiple states under PM Surya Ghar Yojana; rooftop is fully cash business. Targeting tier-2 to tier-4 markets.

guidance_outlook: Micro-irrigation targeted to grow at an average 20-25% over the next three years.
Solar EPC contribution targeted to reach parity with micro-irrigation (50:50 from current ~80:20) within next two years.
Ahmedabad plant expected to lift micro-irrigation EBITDA margin by 1-1.5 percentage points once fully operational this year.
Current capacity can deliver ~INR400 crore micro-irrigation revenue for the next couple of years without additional capex.
Solar pump execution target of at least 1,000 pumps in Q1 FY27.
Working capital intensity expected to stabilise in FY27 on receivable recoveries.
capex_capacity: Ahmedabad facility (about 70,000 sq ft) is now operational; will make high-margin micro-irrigation components in-house.
Existing capacity at Rajkot, Kurnool and Ahmedabad plants supports ~INR400 crore micro-irrigation revenue without new capex.
Management said capex intensity will stay low; working capital is the main capital requirement.
Utilisation is hard to measure because multiple components run on the same extrusion lines; no utilisation figure given.
demand_pricing: Micro-irrigation under-penetration is large: ~70 million hectares potentially addressable, with only ~17-18% penetration achieved so far.
Solar pump order book is concentrated in Maharashtra and is repeat business from state tenders; pump tenders are L1-based with matching rights and quantum allocated by historical execution.
Management expects growth in micro-irrigation mainly from market share gains rather than new dealers or markets.
Network of ~750 dealers used for solar pump and rooftop execution.
Rooftop competition is lower in tier-2 to tier-4 markets, where few quality vendors operate, per management.
Margin pressure from raw material prices in March 2026 due to geopolitical events.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin decline due to the shift toward solar, which may be structurally lower margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline was mainly raw material costs in March; pump margins are similar to micro-irrigation, so there is no mix dilution.

qa_highlights.question: What share of micro-irrigation revenue is cash versus subsidy, and what is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash business was about 15% of micro-irrigation in FY26; rooftop is all cash. Working capital intensity rose with growth and is expected to stabilise on receivable recoveries.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the enhanced INR50 crore SBI credit line is drawn to backstop subsidy delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give the exact drawdown; it said debt was about INR89 crore at March-end and 30-35% of bank limits are unutilised.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Ahmedabad plant add to margins, and will there be a consolidated FY27 margin guide?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-irrigation EBITDA margin is expected to rise 1-1.5 percentage points once the plant is fully running; no consolidated FY27 margin guide was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the growth sustainable given policy and project dependence?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees continued central government support for PM-KUSUM and rooftop schemes and expects growth to persist for a considerable period.

qa_highlights.question: What is the solar pump order book and run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Latest order is 500 pumps (~INR11 crore); ~1,000 pumps were executed in Q4 and at least 1,000 are targeted for the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Can micro-irrigation handle more volume without capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said current capacity supports about INR400 crore of micro-irrigation revenue for the next couple of years.

risks_watch: Raw material price volatility after the March 2026 spike; Q4 margin was 9.96%.
Working capital intensity and receivable recovery from state subsidy disbursements.
Subsidy timing and state-level disbursement cycles; solar pump execution is bound by a 60-day completion window.
Competitive intensity in micro-irrigation and rooftop solar from regional players.
Solar pump order book depends heavily on Maharashtra; new state empanelments under PM-KUSUM are pending.
No disclosed FY27 consolidated margin guidance; export and non-subsidy share still small.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and policy support, with the company's own targets (20-25% micro-irrigation growth, solar parity in two years) stated firmly. More cautious and evasive on finance: declined to give the credit line drawdown and the exact working capital days, and the margin answer leaned on a one-off raw material cost explanation.
key_quotes: So, definitely working capital is something which is fungible and which can be changed.
So, we are only taking an order when we are sure that we are going to execute during that period.
In micro-irrigation business, it is not a tender-based business, it is an impenetrable model.

adds.what: Ahmedabad micro-irrigation component plant (~70,000 sq ft), now operational

growth.why: Management targets micro-irrigation growth of 20-25% average over three years, backed by existing capacity supporting ~INR400 crore revenue without capex, the newly operational Ahmedabad plant, a 500-pump INR11 crore order and a 1,000-pump Q1 FY27 execution target, though no order book or capacity numbers cover the full 20-25% path.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided micro-irrigation EBITDA margin up 1-1.5 percentage points from the Ahmedabad plant in FY27, but Q4 margin was 9.96% (down 86 bps YoY) and raw material costs are volatile, with no consolidated margin guide.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Ahmedabad ~70,000 sq ft micro-irrigation component plant is already operational, and existing Rajkot, Kurnool and Ahmedabad capacity supports ~INR400 crore micro-irrigation revenue for the next couple of years (FY26 total income INR419 crore), so new capacity is in place but no new line has a date.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Micro-irrigation targeted at 20-25% average growth over three years, with ~INR400 crore capacity available without capex and solar pumps at 1,000+ per quarter (Q4 ~1,000 executed, 500-pump ~INR11 crore order in hand), though the order book beyond that is not disclosed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says ~INR400 crore revenue is achievable without additional capex for the next couple of years and that overall capex intensity will stay low; no utilisation figure is given, and no new capex was announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q4 FY26 revenue of INR142 crore was up ~80% YoY and solar pump execution is targeted at 1,000+ pumps in Q1 FY27 (about 1,000 done in Q4), but no numeric guidance was raised and the 20-25% growth target is a three-year average.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 EBITDA margin fell 86 bps YoY to 9.96% on the March raw material spike, receivables and working capital are still stretched, and solar execution depends on subsidy disbursement and a 60-day completion window.

rows.label: Solar rooftop and pump expansion into new states under PM-KUSUM
rows.why: New state empanelments under PM-KUSUM are pending, and the pump order book is concentrated in Maharashtra (~1,500 pumps in FY26), so wider state wins would add volume but are not yet secured.

rows.label: Receivable recovery stabilises working capital
rows.why: Management expects working capital intensity to stabilise in FY27 on receivable recoveries, but debt was INR89 crore at March-end and the drawdown on the INR50 crore SBI line was not disclosed.

rows.label: Bank limits headroom
rows.why: Banks have 30-35% of limits unutilised against INR89 crore of debt, giving headroom, but no debt reduction target was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on micro-irrigation growth targets, solar parity and PM-KUSUM policy support, but cautious and evasive on finance, declining to give the SBI credit line drawdown and exact working capital days, while attributing the margin fall to a one-off March raw material spike.
